direction.comments: The macroscale is a return to his early-2000s blockbuster sci-fi style (A.I., Minority Report, War of the Worlds), which feels like a slight regression from his recent grounded progress (West Side Story, The Fabelmans) but remains highly effective; The microscale is notably stiff, hindered by clunky interpersonal sequences; Storytelling is engaging, relying on his veteran ability to effortlessly capture audience interest; Tension and action sequences are well-directed to serve the narrative

performance.comments: Honestly did the best she could with the script she was given; she definitely displays a good range of emotions, despite her actual dialogue being pretty bad and clunky (which makes her performance feel unnatural at times); has decent chemistry with the cast, which is honestly a plus considering how stiff the interpersonal scenes are

Honestly a step back from the progress he's been making as an actor; his character felt very unnatural and stiff throughout the movie, especially in the interpersonal sequences with Eve Hewson; I get that he is trying to play the nerd character, but it doesn't come off as well as many sequences just feel very disconnected, as if he was taking turns acting with his screen partner
Plays a very templated villain character; even if Spielberg said he isn't the villain, he is very much the villain of this movie.

Just a very stiff performance overall; shares the stiff interpersonal sequences with Josh O'Connor where it blatantly feels like 'he is acting, and then his girlfriend is acting,' which makes their chemistry feel very off

The only performance that was good, absolutely nailing it down; it is a very similar character to his role in Running Man but less showy, maintaining the same gravitas, proving he is definitely one of the top actors currently working in Hollywood.

cast.comments: Most of the performances in this movie feel like they are from inexperienced actors that are not good, heavily hindered by an unnatural and clunky script; this poor script really hurts the chemistry in this movie because it makes the interpersonal scenes feel very stiff.

story.comments: It is very obvious that Spielberg wrote the story because it is not good; The concept is a sci-fi alien movie where you have to suspend your belief, which works fine because this is his bread and butter; The plot structure is a bit of a mess because there is basically no exposition at all; You start right at the inciting incident; Because of this, you do not feel attached to the characters; The rest of the plot structure is fine but is still kind of formulaic (with the ending feeling a little abrupt); Character writing is not great because you do not care for any of these characters, despite how much they are propped up; The character writing is also bad considering they rely on many templated characters, like the villains

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is very unnatural and clunky, which makes this movie feel incredibly stiff (especially in the interpersonal scenes); The humor goes on for way too long because they do not know when to stop a joke, like the phone-smashing scene; The symbolism is very surface-level and topical because of how classified UAPs and alien info are starting to be disclosed, but it is also an analogy for the current treatment of immigrants and "aliens" in this country; Despite its obvious symbolism, this is not a very deep movie because most of the messaging is surface-level (which is fine because this movie is not trying to be too serious); The foreshadowing is pretty formulaic

score.comments: The score feels like a return to form for John Williams because it is well-written and feels like a classic collaboration between Spielberg and Williams (with some Star Wars flavors as well), but it was not used as well as it could have been because it either does not match the tone of the scenes or is too quiet, with the best song being the end-credits song

cinematography.comments: I am not a huge fan of Janusz's dull color grading, which makes the movie feel too much like a movie and not very natural, though they definitely did try some experimental cinematography techniques that did hit (most of the time)

editing.comments: They try a lot of experimental techniques, giving you seamless, cool transitions; It hits a good seven out of ten times, but the three times it does not hit, it is exceptionally egregious

sound.comments: The sound design was pretty standard for a Spielberg blockbuster sci-fi movie

visual_effects.comments: Visual effects are good overall, though there are some moments that feel a little tacky, like the blue screen in the train sequence; It is great to see practical puppeteering used in the movie, which is something I would love to see more of

production_design.comments: The sets for this movie were not very memorable, which is a shame because many of Spielberg's iconic movies were built on iconic sets

review.pacing: Pacing felt unbearably slow; Many sequences went on for too long (such as the phone-smashing sequence, Colin Firth talking to the girlfriend, and seeing the house for the first time), and they could have easily reduced the runtime by twenty to thirty minutes
review.climax: The climax disclosure and the actual ending were enjoyable sequences, but they were hindered by having to spend the entire climax with a news anchor who was just thrust into our lives, making it hard to feel connected
review.tone: The tone felt like Spielberg was trying to have fun and return to his passionate sci-fi and alien roots, but an unnatural script makes it feel very stiff overall
review.overall: Overall, "Disclosure Day" feels like Spielberg returning to a reliable blockbuster format he is used to as he returns to his sci-fi alien roots, which feels like a step back from his recent, more grounded work; while the movie does have that classic Spielberg blockbuster feel with an iconic John Williams score, the movie is heavily hindered by its script that lays out a formulaic story and is filled with clunky dialogue that leads to stiff performances and interpersonal scenes, making the movie feel much longer than it actually is
